tasks.short: Inspect a finished project for safety and compliance

steps.what: Build the checklist from the signed drawing
Inspect the finished work against each clause
Measure the items the engineer names
Draft the finding from recorded inspection rows

loop.input: pass or fail rows and measurements
loop.output: finding that cites clause and location ids
loop.check: Every clause id was on the checklist and every measurement has a location id
loop.stop: One pass, then drop a row with no location
loop.why_not_simpler: Why a fail matters for safety is not a fixed sentence for a clause id

steps.what: Sign the safety and compliance finding
File the signed inspection finding

tasks.design: The checklist is the clause ids on the signed drawing in {DOCS}. The transportation engineer inspects the finished work on site, and the site inspector records measurements with a location id. The finding is drafted only from those rows. The engineer signs it. The visit is not a desk check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inspection notes were free text, so a later reader could not tell which clause and which place had been looked at.
tasks.enabler_now: The signed drawing can supply clause ids, and a field row can store location id, pass or fail, measurement and unit.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing the finished work, and deciding whether it is safe and compliant, stays on site with the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer inspects and signs the finding. A model does not decide compliance.
tasks.altitude: The checklist is ready before the visit. The walk and the compliance decision do not get shorter.

reach.task: Measure items the engineer names on site
reach.learn: Which clause ids are on the checklist and which locations still have no measurement

evidence.claim: Inspecting a finished transport project is a site visit against the drawing. In a mid-size firm the checklist can be prepared. The look cannot.
Digest [S12] and [S13] say safety components in road traffic can be high-risk under the EU AI Act. A model does not decide this safety or compliance finding. The transportation engineer still signs.
Digest [S20] says a research paper was withdrawn because the institution did not trust the data, so a measurement is written into the finding only with a location id.

assumptions: Focal role is the transportation engineer. The task ends when the signed inspection finding is filed. Remedial works are later. This is a visit, not a model check of a drawing.

Input contract: project id, clause id, location id, pass or fail, measurement, unit. Producer of the clause ids is the signed drawing. Producer of the measurements is the site inspector at the engineer's direction. A measurement with no location id is not written into the finding.
Build the checklist from the drawing's clause list with the document store's own fields before custom code. The visit stays manual.
The hours prior is mostly on site. These steps do not treat the walk as saved.
unknowns: Which clauses the authority treats as safety-critical.
Whether the site inspector may record a fail without the engineer present.
research_questions: What share of inspection notes today name no clause id?
How often is a finding changed after the engineer leaves the site?

already_counted.description: Inspection time on site stays with the engineer
Engineer edits the finding before signing
Signature time stays on the finding

incremental.description: Update the checklist fields when a drawing standard adds a clause
Site inspector repeats a measurement the finding rejected

approvals.approved_version: inspection finding signed for this project id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the drawing has no clause ids, so the checklist is still written on site and the walk is unchanged. The high case assumes clause ids exist, while the inspection, the measurements and the signature stay. Remedial construction is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review a development plan for traffic impact

steps.what: Send the development plan for traffic review
Extract land use, accesses and peak trips

loop.output: land use, access count and peak trips with a page
loop.check: Each peak-trip figure cites a page or table id in the plan
loop.stop: One pass, then drop a figure with no page
loop.why_not_simpler: Trip numbers are written in prose and a fixed cell cannot find them

steps.what: Run coded rules for required plan sections
Compare stated trips with the threshold table
Judge the traffic impact and mitigation
Draft the impact note from that judgement

loop.output: note that cites pages and the judgement
loop.check: Every trip figure cites a page that was extracted, and the mitigation matches the judgement
loop.stop: One pass, then stop if the judgement is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: The impact narrative is not a fixed sentence for a threshold row

steps.what: Sign the traffic-impact note
Confirm each cited trip has a page

tasks.design: The development plan arrives by {EMAIL}. Required sections are checked with coded rules. Stated peak trips are extracted only with a page, then compared with the threshold table on a {SPREADSHEET}. The transportation engineer judges the traffic impact and signs the note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trip numbers were retyped from the plan with no page, so a review could not show where a figure came from.
tasks.enabler_now: A plan section can be tested for required headings, and a trip figure can be kept only with a page or table id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the trips are a real impact, and what mitigation is fit, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges the impact. Coded rules do not decide it, and a hearing is not this task.

ambition.what: Issue the impact note when the plan arrives, rather than in a monthly batch

tasks.altitude: Less time checking that a section exists. The impact judgement and the signature stay.

reach.task: Send the next development plan for traffic review
reach.learn: Which plans failed a required section and which trip figures had no page

evidence.claim: Reviewing a development plan for traffic impact is a read of someone else's plan. Completeness can be listed. The impact cannot.
Digest [S5] says a model-checking product for building models runs coded rules. That fits a check that required plan sections exist, not the traffic-impact judgement and not a public hearing.
Digest [S20] says a research paper was withdrawn because the institution did not trust the data, so a peak-trip figure is used only when it cites a page.

assumptions: Focal role is the transportation engineer. The task ends when the signed impact note is issued. Approving the development is the agency's later act.

Input contract: plan id, land-use code, access count, peak trips, page or table id, threshold id. Producer is the agency reviewer with the applicant's plan. A trip figure with no page is dropped. The mitigation choice is produced by the engineer.
Configure coded section rules before custom code. Those rules do not judge the impact.
The hours prior is documents, with some meetings. The judgement meeting stays. The section check is not that meeting.
unknowns: Which threshold table the authority uses.
Whether the applicant may revise trips after the note.
Who presents the note if a hearing follows.
research_questions: What share of stated trip figures have no page?
How often does the engineer reject the applicant's trips?

already_counted.description: Engineer checks extracts that look wrong
Impact judgement time stays with the engineer
Signature time stays on the impact note

incremental.description: Update required-section rules when the authority changes the plan contents
Agency reviewer sends a replacement page for a dropped trip figure

approvals.approved_version: traffic-impact judgement for this plan id
traffic-impact note signed for this plan id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes plans are scanned images with no section ids, so extraction is weak and the engineer still reads the whole plan. The high case assumes sections and pages exist, while the impact judgement and the signature stay. A later public hearing is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate a corridor's traffic system and lighting

steps.what: Read corridor delay and night-crash rows
Line lighting faults up against the corridor
State operating constraints for the corridor
Decide whether the traffic system needs a change
Draft the evaluation from that decision

loop.check: Every delay, night-crash count and fault count cites a row, and the outcome matches the decision
loop.stop: Stop if the decision is missing, and do not invent a second outcome
loop.why_not_simpler: How the corridor is operated is not a fixed sentence for a delay value

steps.what: Check the cited standard clause is current
Sign the system evaluation

tasks.design: Corridor delay, night-crash counts and lighting faults are rows on {BI}. The project controller states operating constraints. The transportation engineer decides whether the traffic system needs a change. A {DOCS} evaluation cites those rows and the decision, and the engineer signs it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Corridor studies mixed device lists and delay tables, so a recommendation could not show which night-crash row it used.
tasks.enabler_now: A corridor id can join delay, night-crash count and lighting fault count in one export the evaluation must cite.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the whole system should change, given how it is operated, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides if the system needs a change. The note may not choose a different outcome.

ambition.what: Reopen the evaluation when night-crash rows move, not only at the annual review

tasks.altitude: The corridor table is no longer rebuilt by hand. The operating constraints and the decision stay in the meeting.

reach.task: State operating constraints for the corridor
reach.learn: Which corridor ids have a signed change decision and which rows were dropped

evidence.claim: Evaluating a transport corridor is a read of delay and crash rows plus a talk about how the system is run. It is not a device-by-device inventory walk.

Digest [S12] and [S13] say safety components in road traffic can be high-risk under the EU AI Act. A model does not decide whether the traffic system must change. The transportation engineer still signs.
Digest [S20] says a research paper was withdrawn because the institution did not trust the data, so a delay or crash figure in the evaluation must cite a row.

assumptions: Focal role is the transportation engineer. The task ends when the signed system evaluation is filed. A device-by-device lighting sample is a different task and is not repeated here.

Input contract: corridor id, mode, delay minutes, night-crash count, lighting fault count, control type. Producer is the operations export. The change-or-not decision is produced by the engineer after the controller states constraints. A row with no corridor id is dropped.
Use the dashboard filters before custom code. The meeting and the decision stay manual.
The hours prior includes a large meeting share. That meeting stays, because the constraints are not a system record until the controller states them.
unknowns: Which corridors have night-crash rows that are complete.
Whether lighting faults are counted on the same system as delay.
Who funds a system change the evaluation names.
research_questions: What share of corridor rows have no night-crash count?
How often does the controller's constraint change the engineer's first view?

already_counted.description: Engineer checks the fault lineup before the meeting
System decision time stays in the meeting
Signature time stays on the evaluation

incremental.description: Keep corridor filters aligned when a new count type is added
Design checker rechecks a clause after the standard is reissued

approvals.approved_version: system-change decision for this corridor id
system evaluation signed for this corridor id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes delay and crash figures are not keyed to a corridor, so the engineer still builds the table and still meets. The high case assumes rows exist, while the constraints meeting, the decision and the signature stay. Installing equipment is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Issue the environmental statement for analysis
List required topics against the sections
Extract stated figures with their page numbers

loop.input: statement sections and the topic list
loop.output: figures each with a page and a topic code
loop.check: Every figure has a page number that exists in the statement and a topic code from the list
loop.stop: One pass, then drop a figure with no page
loop.why_not_simpler: Figures are buried in prose and a fixed table cannot find them

steps.what: Judge whether the statement supports the project
Draft the analysis from tagged extracts only

loop.check: Every figure in the memo equals a tagged extract, and the gaps match the judgement
loop.stop: One pass, then delete a sentence whose figure has no page
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether the statement is adequate is not a fixed sentence for a topic code

steps.what: Sign the environmental analysis
File the signed environmental analysis

tasks.design: The environmental statement is a file in {DOCS}. Required topics are listed from a fixed code list. Stated figures are extracted only with a page number. The transportation engineer judges the gaps and signs the memo. A figure with no page is dropped.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysis memos repeated figures from the statement with no page, so a reviewer could not tell a copied number from an invented one.
tasks.enabler_now: A topic code list can be matched to section headings, and an extract can be required to carry a page before it is used.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the statement supports the project is a reading judgement. Extraction does not make it.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges the gaps and signs. Untagged figures never enter the memo.

ambition.what: Comment on a gap as soon as that section is extracted, rather than after a full reread

tasks.altitude: Less time hunting whether a topic was addressed. The judgement of the statement stays with the engineer.

reach.task: Issue the environmental statement for analysis
reach.learn: Which topic codes had no section and which figures were dropped for lack of a page

evidence.claim: Analysing an environmental statement is a long read. In a mid-size firm the engineer checks topics and figures, then judges whether the statement supports the project.
Digest [S20] says a research paper was withdrawn because the institution did not trust the data, so a model-written figure is never filed in this memo unless it cites a page in the statement.

assumptions: Focal role is the transportation engineer. The task ends when the signed analysis is filed. Writing the statement, and the authority's decision on it, are not this task.

Input contract: statement id, section id, topic code, stated figure, unit, page. Producer is the agency reviewer with the issued statement. A figure with no page is dropped. The gap judgement is produced by the engineer.
Match topic codes with the document store's own headings list before custom code. The judgement meeting stays manual.
The hours prior is mostly the document, plus a meeting. The meeting stays. This is not a building-model check and not an energy or product-safety filing.
unknowns: Which topic code list the authority requires.
Whether figures in appendices count as pages.
Who signs if a specialist discipline owns noise or ecology.
research_questions: What share of figures in past memos have no page?
Which topic codes are most often missing from statements?

already_counted.description: Engineer reviews extracts before relying on them
Gap judgement time stays with the engineer
Signature time stays on the analysis

incremental.description: Update the topic code list when the authority adds a required topic
Agency reviewer supplies a missing page the extract dropped

approvals.approved_version: gap judgement for this statement id
environmental analysis signed for this statement id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the statement is a scan with no section headings, so extraction often fails and the engineer still reads it through. The high case assumes headings and pages exist, while the gap judgement and the signature stay. Preparing the statement itself is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Visits and judgements stay on site and in the review, while checklists and extracts come from the record.
reach: The site inspector records measurements against clause ids the engineer set for the visit.
The agency reviewer receives an impact note or an environmental memo where every figure has a page.
skills_to_grow: Inspect against a checklist taken from the signed drawing.
Refuse a trip number or an environmental figure that has no page.
Judge a corridor from delay and crash rows rather than from a device inventory.
role.ambitious_version: A finished project has a signed inspection finding, and no environmental figure is filed without the page it came from.
